competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — Duck Harness technical overview
competitorFacts.text: Tufa Labs says its public Duck harness lets an LLM inspect game grids as image and text, write Python in a REPL, and keep context short by evicting older messages. This describes the published Milestone 1 system, not an unverified current submission.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize places Argon behind Astra’s 99.9% ARC-AGI-3 result. It reports 62% fewer actions than the human baseline on the 25 public games, matching or beating three speedrun records and coming within 10% on six others.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Keep the public-demo action comparison separate from the semi-private Verified score.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize says API issues prevented complete standard-harness testing: low reasoning completed 42/55 games for 49.8%; medium completed 46/55 for 46.3%; high completed 19/55 and no score was published. Reported scores retain partial credit across all 55 games. Provider adapter preserves opaque reasoning and permits automatic compaction; standard harness carries notes between turns. Costs use introductory $2 input/$10 output per million tokens.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Material limit on harness comparisons. Do not present incomplete standard-harness runs as a clean capability ceiling.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announces Gemini 4 Argon Verified results: ARC-AGI-3 97.5% at $4.8K with the provider adapter and 49.8% at $5.8K with the standard harness; ARC-AGI-2 91.3% at $0.32/task and ARC-AGI-1 98.5% at $0.16/task. It calls Google DeepMind the second frontier lab above 95% on ARC-AGI-3.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Consequential organizer result. Separate from Kaggle standings. Standard-harness API incompletion is essential context; primary results introduction says 91.2% on v2 while its table and announcement say 91.3%.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize’s October 13 announcement reports DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at about 3% with its provider adapter and below 1% with the standard harness. The original linked verified-results table, refreshed October 14, gives a matched Low-reasoning comparison of 3.26% versus 0.35%; its headline best configurations differ in reasoning level. Organizer model evaluation, separate from Kaggle team submissions.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Public original read without sign-in in the in-app browser; linked primary results table independently read. Organizer evaluation, separate from Kaggle team standings.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announces Tufa Labs reclaimed first on the ARC-AGI-3 public Kaggle board with roughly 69%, up from roughly 56%. This is the author’s dated October 13 observation; refresh standings before publication.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Organizer confirmation of a consequential team result already covered in the newspaper’s morning/afternoon reporting; no methods disclosed.

socialPosts.author: AlexBarry4
socialPosts.summary: Replying to Psyho’s PuzzleScript benchmark announcement, Barry says Epoch might be able to support API costs and that he has sent a DM. This is a tentative public statement; no funding agreement or collaboration is established.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: New response to the archive’s independent benchmark lead; recheck any later public confirmation before describing support as secured.

socialPosts.author: GregKamradt
socialPosts.summary: Kamradt publicly replies that he sent a DM to Psyho after Psyho announced a nearly finished private PuzzleScript-based reasoning benchmark.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Organizer interest in an independent game benchmark; the message contents and any collaboration are unknown.

socialPosts.author: FakePsyho
socialPosts.summary: Asked about online solutions and prior model knowledge, Psyho says the selected games are niche and that reviewing logs for all selected games revealed no suspicious behavior.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Author-reported contamination check; does not independently establish absence of training exposure.

socialPosts.author: FakePsyho
socialPosts.summary: Psyho reports full-run costs of $700 for Sol 6.1 and $60 for Luna 6, and estimates about $1,000 for Sonnet 5.5 and $4,000 for Astra 6. Says testing uses xhigh and may reduce generous action limits to lower cost.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Separates reported completed costs from forecasts; no logs, scores or reproducible release verified.

socialPosts.author: FakePsyho
socialPosts.summary: Psyho says a nearly finished PuzzleScript benchmark selects 40 games from over 300, uses Codex/Claude Code harnesses with code generation prohibited, and keeps the game set private. The author says generous action limits already allow some saturation while models remain inefficient.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Potential benchmark-development story; author claims, not an official ARC release or independently verified score.

socialPosts.author: mhmazur
socialPosts.summary: Mazur says that, based on conversations with some lab staff and to the best of his knowledge, none have built synthetic RL environments specifically to raise ARC scores. He explains that ARC calls datasets semi-private because evaluation data leaves the organization through third-party model APIs, despite zero data retention.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Follow-up to the evaluation-integrity exchange. Attribute to Mazur; this is not an independent audit of lab training data. The critic acknowledges having no evidence of that practice.

socialPosts.author: mhmazur
socialPosts.summary: Responding to an allegation that benchmarks test on training data, Mazur says ARC is not compromised, its semi-private evaluation sets have not leaked and cannot be trained on, and provider API testing requires zero data retention.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Useful organizer statement on evaluation integrity; attribute to Mazur rather than presenting it as an independent audit.

dispatches.headline: It’s official: Team Turducken is born as Keith Tyser’s ARC Slayers join Son, Mark and Ronen

image.alt: Team Turducken’s full crew works on a giant mechanical turkey containing a mechanical chicken and a duck in sunglasses, in a glowing hangar overlooking snowy mountains and a castle. Mark works on the wing, Son tends the cockpit, and Keith’s yellow mascot uses a tablet beside two armoured Yorkies. DZ, a blonde chibi girl holding a pink bunny, operates diagnostics; NT, a tabby kitten in a banana costume shedding comic tears, adjusts a thruster; Choryu, a technician with a cardiac MRI display for a head, connects cables; and Herminator, Ronen’s silver knight bot with a cobalt-blue plume, tightens the mech’s fittings. All wear matching tech harnesses.
image.caption: Team Turducken’s official artwork.

sections.heading: Off the gossip wire, onto the record
sections.text: Yesterday the gossip desk had only a whisper. Today it has the paperwork. Son Pham’s ARC-3 team—Son Pham, Mark Barney and Ronen—has merged with Keith Tyser’s team, the ARC Slayers. Son sent the formal Kaggle team invite and the Slayers accepted. The champagne we told you to keep on ice can come out.

sections.heading: Who is on the roster
sections.text: From Son’s side: Son Pham, Mark Barney and Ronen. From the ARC Slayers: Keith Tyser, NT (mitubant on Kaggle), dzj (Chris-440 on GitHub) and kawaimahiro. Son is coordinating the combined team’s submissions.

sections.heading: The name: Team Turducken
sections.text: The naming drama is settled. The merged squad rolls out as Team Turducken: three crews nested into one bird, the way a chicken goes inside a duck inside a turkey. Son says the name is also partly a tip of the hat to the Tufa team and to Daniel Franzen, whose public work the squad builds on. The Digest notes, with no small satisfaction, that a duck inside a duck inside a bird was already our branding department’s pick. Team Allegedly may now retire with honour.

sections.heading: Disclosure
sections.text: Mark Barney, the Digest’s head human editor, is a member of the merged team. These facts come from the team’s own messages on 18 October; the public leaderboard will reflect the merged roster once it refreshes. The artwork is the team’s own and is imaginative, not documentary.
